judgment_calls: SHARP-EDGE HAZARD VERDICT (requested by dispatch): PostApplyEvent.preChangeSnapshotJson IS run through redactSecrets() at write time (post_apply_events_repository.ts createAsync/updateStatusAsync), same as alert_payload_json. If it were ever used as the restoration source for a live config write, a secret-shaped priorValue would restore as the literal string '[redacted]' — real corruption. This service does NOT use preChangeSnapshotJson for restoration at all; it restores from AgentOrgProposal.beforeSnapshotJson (a separate column on agent_org_proposals), which is NEVER routed through redactSecrets (confirmed: only post_apply_events_repository.ts imports/calls redactSecrets; agent_org_proposals_repository.ts does not). Pinned by the 'sharp edge' test, which plants a Bearer-shaped string as a system_prompt priorValue and asserts the restored live config equals it byte-exact (not '[redacted]'). Conclusion: NOT a hazard for this implementation. Follow-up worth filing: if a future caller (D2.5) ever repurposes preChangeSnapshotJson as a restoration source instead of the documented opaque CAS pointer, it will hit exactly this corruption bug — the model's own doc comment already warns against this, but there's no type-level enforcement.

SECOND SHARP EDGE FOUND (not asked for, but load-bearing for this implementation): org_proposal_apply.ts's revertProposal() — the codebase's own existing generic revert primitive, and the naive candidate for 'the existing CAS revert path' — cannot be reused here. Its containsScopeBearingPayload() legacy-scope guard refuses ANY changeJson whose payload contains `agentConfigId` alongside a `field`/`value` key anywhere in the object tree, unless the beforeSnapshotJson also carries a scope-v2 `version` tag. That is exactly the shape refineConfigApplier's own validator requires for a machine-applyable refine-config patch ('a machine-applyable configPatch {agentConfigId, field, value}') and the shape D2.3's repair proposals use. Empirically confirmed: containsScopeBearingPayload({configPatch:{agentConfigId,field:'model',value:'x'}}) === true. Routing this service's real-world changeJson through revertProposal would refuse EVERY revert as 'unsafe-legacy-scope'. Worked around by calling the same underlying exported primitives revertProposal's own isConfigFieldSnapshot branch uses (agentConfigFieldPatch, readAgentConfigField, projectAgentProfileAfterWrite with cause 'scope-revert') directly, bypassing the buggy gate — not by modifying revertProposal itself (out of scope for D2.4; the gap looks pre-existing and would also affect a human's #857 manual /revert of any refine-config proposal with a full field+value configPatch, independent of this feature — worth its own follow-up issue).

Restoration requires the proposal state machine's applied -> measuring hop (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS forbids applied -> reverted directly) before it can reach 'reverted'. That transition is CAS-guarded with expectedRevision = the proposal's own revision read moments earlier — this IS the drift/conflict detector for issue-1434-c2 (a concurrently-touched original proposal, e.g. a human revert or the unrelated org-optimizer measure sweep picking it up first, fails this check and/or the preceding proposal.status !== 'applied' guard, never silently clobbering whatever state it's actually in).

Alert payload (`{proposalId, profileId, changeType, originalChange, repairAttempts, revert, generatedAt}`) is written through PostApplyEventsRepository.updateStatusAsync, which already redacts alert_payload_json via redactSecrets before persisting — this service does not redact manually, it relies on the existing repository-level guard (same defense-in-depth precedent documented on the PostApplyEvent model).
No existing file was modified — auto_revert_service.ts and its test are the only two new files, per the dispatch's explicit expectation.

SECURITY FOLLOW-UP FIX (post-review, same session's contract, second pass): the ORIGINAL implementation above missed that org_proposal_apply.ts's revertProposal() refuses a whole-field revert of allowedMcpsJson/allowedSkillsJson/corePermissionsJson ('unsafe-legacy-scope') — a guard this service's direct-helper-reuse strategy silently bypassed, since it calls agentConfigFieldPatch/readAgentConfigField directly rather than through revertProposal. allowedSkillsJson is a real reachable target: it is in CONFIG_PATCH_FIELDS (a legal refine-config repair target used by D2.3's own auto-repair) AND in the refused set. Fixed by exporting UNSAFE_WHOLE_FIELD_SCOPE_FIELDS from org_proposal_apply.ts (previously an inline literal in the revertProposal else-if) and adding the identical refusal check in auto_revert_service.ts before the field restore, so both paths share one source of truth and can never drift. allowedDelegatesJson (also in CONFIG_PATCH_FIELDS) is deliberately NOT in the refused set, matching revertProposal's existing established scope exactly — not tightened beyond it. Falsification: the new regression test was confirmed to fail (outcome 'reverted' instead of 'revert_failed', live config silently clobbered) with the guard temporarily disabled, then confirmed green again with it restored.

ROOT-CAUSE FIX (third session, this dispatch): the 'second sharp edge' from the first session — 'revertProposal cannot be reused, containsScopeBearingPayload refuses every configPatch{agentConfigId,field,value}' — was itself the bug, not a fixed constraint to route around. Root cause: at org_proposal_apply.ts's revertProposal() line ~741 (`isScopeBearing = isScopeMutationKind || containsScopeBearingPayload(change)`), `change` for a refine-config proposal is the RAW changeJson `{configPatch:{agentConfigId,field,value}}`. containsScopeBearingPayload treats a bare {agentConfigId,field,value} object as scope-bearing on its own (target=true via the agentConfigId key, operation=true via the field+value keys, at ANY depth in the tree — combine() propagates a child's `detected` upward regardless of the parent's own keys), so this was true unconditionally for every refine-config revert, never reaching the isConfigFieldSnapshot restore branch (~951) or the UNSAFE_WHOLE_FIELD_SCOPE_FIELDS refusal branch (~946) that already existed for exactly this snapshot shape.

The apply path (org_proposal_apply_service.ts's strictChangeJsonPreflight, lines ~248-283 before this fix) already solved the identical problem for its own refine-config gate: it narrows past a validated configPatch (splitting it out of the payload, re-attaching agentConfigId to the remainder) before running containsScopeBearingPayload on 'everything outside the patch'. Extracted that inline narrowing into a new exported function, extractValidatedConfigPatch(parsed), shared by BOTH modules — org_proposal_apply_service.ts's preflight now calls it instead of hand-rolling the same logic, and org_proposal_apply.ts's revertProposal calls it too. 'Validated' is stricter than the apply path's original inline check: extractValidatedConfigPatch additionally requires configPatch.field to be a genuine CONFIG_PATCH_FIELDS member (org_diagnosis_types.ts:116), not just any {agentConfigId,field,value}-shaped object with no extra keys — a malformed/unrecognized field now fails closed (no narrowing, full-payload scope check) rather than silently narrowing. Verified this stricter check does not regress any existing passing test: grepped every configPatch.field value used across the test suite (model, allowedSkillsJson, system_prompt, temperature) and confirmed the one non-CONFIG_PATCH_FIELDS value ('temperature') only appears in org_proposal_experiment_service.test.ts, which tests reserveRunEnrollment, not strictChangeJsonPreflight/validateProposalChange — unaffected.

No circular import risk: org_proposal_apply_service.ts (and its own imports — scope_mutation_contract.ts, strict_json.ts, org_diagnosis_types.ts) do not import org_proposal_apply.ts anywhere, so org_proposal_apply.ts importing extractValidatedConfigPatch FROM org_proposal_apply_service.ts is a one-directional edge. Confirmed by grep before adding the import.

Test-by-test review of every pre-existing assertion the dispatch flagged as currently expecting revertProposal(...) === 'unsafe-legacy-scope' (org_proposal_apply.test.ts lines ~262,343,587,614,746; w1_corrective_4_contract.test.ts line ~364): ALL SIX use a scope-mutation proposal kind (tighten-scope/prune-scope/refine-scope/broaden-scope), where `isScopeMutationKind` is already true and short-circuits `isScopeBearing` to true via the `||` regardless of the containsScopeBearingPayload narrowing — none of them exercise a refine-config (or any other non-scope-kind) changeJson shaped like a configPatch, so NONE of them were affected by this fix. auto_revert_service.ts's interim UNSAFE_WHOLE_FIELD_SCOPE_FIELDS guard (added second pass, session 631c9409) is DELETED. runAutoRevertAsync now: (1) still performs its own CAS-guarded applied->measuring transition (revertProposal does not do this hop — ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS forbids applied->reverted directly, and revertProposal expects a proposal already at a revertable status), then (2) calls revertProposal(measuring, {proposalsRepo, configsRepo}) for the actual restore/refusal + the final measuring->reverted transition, then (3) keeps an independent post-write verification (re-reading the live field and comparing to the snapshot's priorValue) as defense-in-depth on top of revertProposal's own write. revertProposal's own UNSAFE_WHOLE_FIELD_SCOPE_FIELDS branch now supplies the exact same refusal the interim guard used to hand-roll — mapped onto 'revert_failed' with {reason:'unsafe-legacy-scope', field, proposalId}, matching the existing alert/status contract.
